statement: A token's tenant claim names a tenant or is absent. Absent, the principal is in the default tenant (0). An empty claim makes the token invalid (401 token-invalid) on every path that verifies one, the pipeline's and refresh's, whichever verifier read it: read as no tenant, it would put the principal in the default tenant with the token's roles. A claim that cannot name a tenant document (blank, `*`, holding `:` or a control character, longer than 128 characters: the rule of `SnapshotKey.Tenant`) makes the token invalid as well, and an API key record with such a tenant fails (503), so every credential applies one rule. CoSec's issuer refuses to sign a token with an empty tenant or one it would refuse.
